pages.name: Don Sebastian (the Ghouled Prince of Los Angeles)

text.content: Don Sebastian Juan Dominguez was a mortal rancho owner near the pueblo of Los Angeles who fled his own home in 1828 after the frenzying @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} elder Christopher Houghton slaughtered his family and made him a ghoul. For over a century Don Sebastian ruled Los Angeles as Christopher's unwitting "front man," secretly Blood Bound and utterly loyal, crowned Prince by his hidden master in 1870. Under his rule the city became a magnet for the most decadent Kindred in America, and his careless indulgence of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} poseurs and casual cruelty toward the growing anarch population — including a savage beating of Jeremy MacNeil in 1943 — finally triggered the 1944 Revolt. Salvador Garcia is publicly credited with killing Don Sebastian in single combat, but Christopher Houghton himself struck the actual killing blow, a secret only Salvador, Jeremy, and a since-vanished @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} witness ever knew.

A @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} elder present at the Boston Massacre, Marguerite Foccart Embraced the dying Crispus Attucks on the spot rather than let his charisma and advocacy for freedom go to waste. She fought beside him through the Revolutionary War and beyond, eventually traveling to Los Angeles to aid Jeremy MacNeil's uprising against Don Sebastian. She also sired the surfer-anarch Steve Booth, though her attempts to mold him into an ideologue mostly failed — he has instead become an easygoing, popular baron in his own right, to her continuing mild disappointment.

Sired reluctantly by Marguerite Foccart, who hoped to build another dedicated revolutionary, Steve Booth instead became a laid-back surfer whose easy charisma and total command of the Long Beach coastline earned him unquestioned loyalty from the local surfer-vampire population. Within his barony Steve's word is absolute; outside it, he has almost no interest in the wider politics of the Free States, to the chronic frustration of both his sire and the scheming @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} David Geduld, who covets his territory.

Born into slavery around 1730 of African and Native American parentage, Crispus Attucks escaped to become a sailor and a leading voice for American liberty in Boston, dying (and being Embraced on the spot by Marguerite Foccart) at the 1770 Boston Massacre. He fought the Redcoats, ran the Underground Railroad, and battled @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} plantation-owners through the Civil War era before traveling west to help Jeremy MacNeil overthrow Don Sebastian in 1944. He now serves the Free States as Jeremy's most trusted enforcer and "muscle," respected by the movers and shakers of Los Angeles even as rank-and-file anarchs dismiss him as merely "one of MacNeil's boys."

A runaway from Chicago who found her calling among the punk anarch scene at the Succubus Club, Ariane (born Jane) drifted to Hollywood and was Embraced by an anarch named Cal at only fourteen apparent years old. She has almost no political awareness or ambition, living only for loud music, wild dancing, and the Hunger — a useful template for the Storyteller wishing to represent the Free States' many young, apolitical street Kindred.

A husband-and-wife pair of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel} sired by the Iconoclast Thrasher, Walter and Millie Gaspars live a quiet unlife on a small ranch in Newhall, largely disconnected from Free States politics. Millie in particular has grown from a terrified fledgling into a confident, self-possessed woman over the past decade and has begun to wonder if other Kindred outside her marriage might be worth knowing.

pages.name: Sir Ralph Hamilton and the European Idealist Delegation

text.content: Sir Ralph Hamilton leads a delegation of London @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} "Idealists" who have come to Los Angeles to study the Free States as a cautionary tale, hoping to find weaknesses that could be used to discourage similar anarch movements from destabilizing the wider clan. His companions include the academic Prof. Habersohn (a Swedish sociologist Embraced specifically to study how societies govern themselves, who has grown surprisingly sympathetic to the anarch cause), the battle-scarred Takuya (a veteran of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} intrigues in the fall of the Soviet Union), and Countess Andrea Visconti (brought along as an afterthought by her husband Count Luigi Visconti, but who has since become the delegation's most effective advocate for anarch philosophy). Sir Ralph is particularly hostile toward Louis Fortier, whom he regards as a class traitor.

Amethyst runs a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} gang out of Santa Ana with the help of her lieutenant Rose (whose beauty and manipulation skills recruit new members) and the young hacker Zipper, whom Rose discovered and brought into the fold. Zipper has recently penetrated the computer systems of Sunburst International, a Pentex subsidiary, and is quietly working to decipher strange files he found there — a thread the Storyteller can use to tie the Free States into wider Pentex or Weaver-adjacent plots.

Bela is a monstrously deformed, almost feral @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} treated as a figure of dark comedy by most of the Free States' Kindred — in any @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} city he would likely have been destroyed as a Masquerade risk, but Los Angeles's anarchs simply leave him be. Alonzo is a reclusive, hideously ugly and disagreeable @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} living in the hills behind the Vignes mansion in Pasadena; one of the rare Nosferatu who has managed to overcome the clan's natural paranoia enough to make outside contact, he has secretly begun teaching forbidden lore to Vera Vignes and her Blood Bound lover Henry Waters.

Identical elderly twin sisters (one with silver hair, one bluish, both actually wigs to heighten the confusion) who murdered their abusive father and became sadistic torturers of Kindred and kine alike, the Blount sisters have converted their Glendale mansion and its hillside shed into an elaborate house of horrors filled with inventive traps. They compete against each other for the most creative and prolonged torture of captured victims, and their ongoing disappearances of local Kindred have begun to worry Jeremy MacNeil, even as the sisters remain unsuspected social acquaintances of the Vignes family.

Edward Vignes is a rigid, old-fashioned 9th-generation @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} elder who has weathered every upheaval in Los Angeles from a position of quiet, rarely-exercised influence at his Pasadena mansion, respected enough that Free States leaders listen when he deigns to offer advice. His wife of over 150 years, Vera Vignes, has recently and unexpectedly fallen in love with their mutual servant Henry Waters, Dominating him into a Blood Bond with her even though he remains Blood Bound to Edward as well. The resulting three-way tangle of loyalty and desire is slowly dissolving Henry's bond to Edward, and the couple has begun secretly consulting the reclusive @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} Alonzo for help escaping Edward's reach.

An English butler Embraced in the 1890s by Edward Vignes to serve the family for eternity, Henry Waters has spent over a century in devoted, Blood-Bound service, until his master's wife Vera fell in love with him and Bound him to her in turn. Torn between loving Edward as a Blood Bound servant and Vera as a secret lover, Henry increasingly fantasizes about fleeing with Vera — a plan that would provoke Edward's full and formidable wrath if it ever came to pass.

A @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} lawyer Embraced in Chicago to manage that city's business interests for the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}, David Geduld was sent to Los Angeles in 1963 to infiltrate and report on the Free States, posing as a rogue @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} fugitive. Amazed to discover a stable, functioning society without princes or primogen, David's loyalties shifted permanently during the 1965 @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} siege, when he fought alongside the anarchs he had once despised. He now rules Torrance as a genuine anarch baron, though older anarchs like Jeremy MacNeil and Crispus Attucks distrust his Ventrue blood, and his Ventrue instincts still drive him to quietly scheme for control of Steve Booth's Long Beach barony.

Believed by most to be Salvador Garcia's childe, Jesus Ramirez is actually a Nicaraguan Kindred created and Blood Bound by the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} Don Cristian de Leon Negro; when his master was killed by @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah}-led Sandinistas in 1978, Jesus fled north to the Free States. Salvador recognized leadership potential in him and took him under his wing, and Jesus now serves as the de facto day-to-day leader of El Hermandad whenever Salvador travels, widely respected as a clear-headed counterbalance to his more emotional mentor and friend.

Gloria appears to be an ordinary, influential @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} operating out of a Whittier poolhall, well-regarded at the Rants for her considered judgment. In truth she is merely the most prominent of several secret agents planted throughout the Free States by a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} Justicar named Petrodon, feeding intelligence on the anarch movement back to the sect leadership.

Dawn built a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ssX4b2JFXF2uegC3]{Followers of Set} temple in Los Angeles that drew Kindred worshippers with promises of forbidden pleasures, until a coterie of young vampires acting on information from her disillusioned acolyte Nicholas tracked her down; Jeremy MacNeil's forces destroyed most of her temple and (apparently) Nicholas along with it, but Dawn herself escaped to Chicago. The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ssX4b2JFXF2uegC3]{Followers of Set} have since rebuilt with two new temples in Los Angeles (one in Beverly Hills, one in the Encino hills), and persistent rumors hold that Dawn has returned seeking vengeance against her former acolyte, Jeremy, and the coterie that exposed her.

pages.name: Mohammed's Lieutenants and the Crypt's Sons

text.content: The Crypt's Sons are Mohammed al-Muthlim's @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra}-led anarch gang, based around a South Central Los Angeles cemetery and controlling both a Kindred following and a powerful allied mortal street gang. Henry "Slash" Taylor, one of Mohammed's most trusted lieutenants, was initiated as a teenager on a dare in the same Inglewood Park Cemetery crypt Mohammed still favors as a haven; totally loyal to his sire-in-all-but-blood, Slash knows little of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}'s true plans but understands he serves its eventual "liberation" of Los Angeles.

vtmlarp.source: Los Angeles by Night, Chapters Two, Four & Five
